content.title: About
content.content: Fruit salad without citrus is a mix of fresh berries, apples, pears, bananas and other non‑citrus fruits, dressed with a light salad sauce or mayonnaise. It is ideal for those who avoid acidic flavors but still want a bright fruit taste and nutritional benefits.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad is popular in summer because it refreshes without any cooking.
Dressings often use a light yogurt‑mustard base or classic mayonnaise for a creamy texture.
Apple and pear slices stay crisp thanks to a splash of apple‑cider vinegar instead of citrus juice.
Bananas add natural sweetness, allowing the recipe to use less added sugar.
The salad can be prepared ahead, but the dressing should be added just before serving to prevent fruit browning.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Apples, pears and bananas provide B1, B2, B6 vitamins that support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: The fruit mix supplies both soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries such as strawberry and blueberry are high in anthocyanins, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Potassium from bananas and apples helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Combining fruit sugars with a light dressing provides quick energy without a sharp glucose spike.

items.title: Fruit allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific fruits like strawberries or kiwi.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The natural sweetness can affect blood sugar levels; people with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Even without citrus, certain fruits (e.g., kiwi) can be acidic and irritate the stomach.

items.title: Mayonnaise content
items.content: If mayonnaise is used, the dish can become calorie‑dense and contain trans fats; opt for a light version or a substitute.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, sprinkled with chopped nuts or seeds. It works as a standalone dish, a side for meat or fish, or as a filling for sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Store the dressing separately to maintain fruit texture.
